links.note: Same definition: CBLM 11 p.8 'the environment or setting in which the assessment activity takes place'. CBLM 11 lists different contents (physical setting, tools, materials, purpose) from CBLM 12 (environment, relationship to real work, time period); that CBLM 11 list is taught in assessment-context-elements. Minor wording difference: p.8 says the environment 'should be prepared', answer key p.26 says 'may be prepared'.
Same two forms of evidence; CBLM 11 p.21 gives the same direct and indirect definitions and examples as CBLM 12 p.17.

Same topic. Contradiction: CBLM 11 p.22 names five rules (Valid, Sufficient, Current, Consistent, Authentic) but then describes six (adds Recency). CBLM 11 p.23 says recent = less than three years old; CBLM 12 p.20 says less than five years. Per-rule checks are taught in checking-evidence-rules. CBLM 11 adds a third count (five) to the decisions.md VSCA (four) decision.

Same topic. CBLM 11 p.12 examples (reader, interpreter, attendant carer, scribe, special equipment, adaptive technology, shorter sessions, large print) overlap CBLM 12's list; p.18 defines it as choosing alternative assessment methods or tools. CBLM 11 adds 'scribe' and 'large print', and spells 'attendant carer' correctly.
Same topic: CBLM 11 p.52-53 gives the same six methods, six tools and four purposes of evidence gathering tools as CBLM 12 p.17-18.
